column4: owner note

THE HILTON NEAR PORTSMOUTH — named in the standing goal. OWNER 2026-09-24, after a rebuild attempt: "It is a single wing, no multiple wings. BUT it is a Y with the two legs going to the ground, narrowing into a tower. Think of turning a Y upside down, then extruding it. The two Y shaped faces are plain concrete, while the windows are on the extruded sides. this is a unique (ugly) building but extremely prominent because it adjoins Portsmouth, the open space in the center of Chinatown. Think Fermilab". So: an inverted-Y PROFILE extruded horizontally, with a real void at ground level between the two splayed legs; blank concrete on the two profile faces, glazing on the swept sides. Zero reference frames exist for this id anywhere in docs/shots/refs — the first rebuild invented a three-winged Y in plan, the second invented a plain slab, both from a web search that said "rectangular" (which described the PLAN). A photograph would settle it; see docs/PHOTOS-NEEDED.md.
